CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding (high blood sugar).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
John is a 55-year-old male with past medical history of anxiety and epilepsy who presents following an emergency room visit for elevated blood sugar. Patient reports he has been traveling and hosting visitors over the past couple of weeks. He was not monitoring his sugar intake and experienced stress and strain during this time. His hemoglobin A1c was borderline in the past but is now elevated. He was started on metformin in the emergency room and has been treated with IV fluids. Since discharge, he reports feeling "so far so good." Regarding anxiety, he had some difficult moments but states things are now better as the weekend approaches and he feels things are under control. Regarding epilepsy, he denies seizures for quite a few months with only a minor episode noted previously.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Denies recent fever or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety, Epilepsy

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice a day (initiated in emergency room). Keppra for epilepsy.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent frequent travel with multiple events and visitors over the past couple of weeks, associated with increased stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Good. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Trace pitting edema noted in lower extremities, likely from IV fluids received in emergency room.

RESULTS
Blood glucose: 162 mg/dL (obtained during this visit; patient ate approximately 2 hours prior).
Hemoglobin A1c: 8 (previous hemoglobin A1c was approximately 6 when patient was not on medications).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed diabetes: Continue metformin 500 mg twice a day with planned increase over time. Order hemoglobin A1c for future monitoring.
2. Anxiety: Discussed potential issues with seasonal changes. Patient willing to try new interventions.
3. Epilepsy: Continue Keppra. Patient to follow up with neurology; last visit was approximately 3 months ago.
